# How to Create Custom Images with Copilot for Invites and Social Posts

> **In short:** Copilot can turn a plain sentence into a custom image you can use on invitations, Instagram, or a personal vision board. Sign in with a Microsoft account, open the Designer tool, describe what you want in plain words, and download what comes out.

You don't need Photoshop, Canva, or any design background to get a one-of-a-kind picture for your next event, post, or vision board. Copilot's built-in image generator — Microsoft Designer — takes a sentence from you and turns it into a finished image in roughly 30 seconds. This walkthrough shows the whole flow, including what to write so the picture actually comes out the way you imagined.

## Before you start
- A **free Microsoft account** (the same one you use for Outlook, OneDrive, or Xbox). If you don't have one, signing up takes about two minutes.
- A **browser** (Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox) or the **Copilot mobile app**. Either works.
- Roughly **10–15 minutes** for your first picture — faster once you've done it a few times.
- The image generator is free to use, but the free plan has a **daily limit** on how many images you can create. If you want a lot more images or faster generation, look into the paid **Microsoft Copilot Pro** plan on Microsoft's official pricing page for the current rate.

## Step 1 — Open Copilot and switch to image mode
Go to **copilot.microsoft.com** in your browser, or open the Copilot app on your phone. Sign in with your Microsoft account if you aren't already. Look for a chat box near the bottom of the screen that says something like **"Ask me anything…"** — and right next to it, find a small **image or picture icon** 🖼️, or a toggle labeled **"Designer"** or **"Create an image."** Tap or click that option. The chat box changes to invite an image description instead of a question, and a small note about Microsoft's content policy may pop up the first time.
💬 Example: don't type anything yet — just make sure you can see the image-creation prompt box.
You'll know it worked when the chat box now asks you to **describe an image** instead of asking a question.

## Step 2 — Describe the picture you actually want
Click inside the new prompt box and write a sentence or two describing your image. Be specific: include the **subject**, the **style** (watercolor, photo-realistic, cartoon, flat design), the **mood** (cheerful, calm, dreamy), and the **colors** if they matter. The more detail you give, the closer the result matches what you imagined. If your screen looks different, look for a separate **"Designer" link** in the top menu, or a button labeled something like **"Image creator"** — Microsoft moves these around as they update the site.
💬 Example: "A watercolor birthday invitation background with soft pink peonies, gold confetti, and the words 'Emma turns 30' written in elegant script at the top."
You'll know it worked when you hit Enter and Copilot starts **generating four different versions** of your image — this usually takes 15–30 seconds.

## Step 3 — Review the four versions and pick your favorite
When the images finish loading, you'll see a grid of **four square images**, all based on your description. Don't rush — open each one in full size by clicking it, and check the small details that matter for your project: is the text readable, are the colors right, does the mood fit the occasion? If none of them are quite right, you don't need to start over — go back to the prompt box and describe what you'd change. Copilot can run another round based on your new description.
💬 Example: "Same image but make the peonies larger, and put the text 'Emma turns 30 — Saturday June 14' in the center."
You'll know it worked when at least one of the new four images is **close enough to use**, or when you've nailed down exactly which change to ask for next.

## Step 4 — Polish the prompt if the text in the image looks wrong
Here's an honest limitation: image generators — Copilot included — are **still hit-or-miss at writing words inside pictures**. Names, dates, and quotes can come out misspelled, scrambled, or warped. If your invite or vision board needs accurate text (like a name or a date), the safest workflow is to **leave the text out of the prompt entirely**, then add it yourself later in a free tool like Canva, PowerPoint, or even your phone's photo editor. This is one extra step, but it guarantees your text actually says what it should.
💬 Example: for the invite, ask for "A watercolor birthday invitation background with soft pink peonies and gold confetti, no text." Then you add "Emma turns 30 — Saturday June 14" yourself.
You'll know it worked when you have a beautiful background image **without any text problems to fix**.

## Step 5 — Download the image you want to use
Hover your cursor over the image you like best. A small toolbar appears underneath — look for a **download icon** (a downward arrow into a tray) or a button labeled **"Download"**. Click it once. Your browser saves the image to your normal Downloads folder, usually as a PNG or JPG file. On the phone app, the download button might say **"Save"** or look like a square with an arrow — if you can't find it, take a screenshot instead, which works on every phone.
💬 Example: click the **Download** button below your favorite peony image and wait for the file to appear in your Downloads folder.
You'll know it worked when you can open the file on your computer or phone and see the finished picture, ready to drop into your design.

## Step 6 — Drop the picture into your project
Open whichever tool you normally use — Canva, PowerPoint, Google Slides, Instagram, your phone's photo editor — and **import or insert** the image you just downloaded. Resize it to fit your canvas: square (1:1) for Instagram, portrait (9:16) for stories, landscape (16:9) for invitations printed on letter-size paper. If you want a different shape than the square Copilot gave you, you can either crop with the same tools or describe a different aspect ratio in Step 2 next time (some Copilot versions accept hints like "wide landscape format" or "tall poster format").
💬 Example: in Canva, click **"Uploads"**, drag in your downloaded peony image, drop it onto a square Instagram template, and add the text "Emma turns 30 — details in bio" on top.
You'll know it worked when your finished design **looks unique to you** and is ready to send, post, or print.

## Common mistakes
- **Asking for text inside the image.** Image generators often misspell names and dates. Strip the text out of the prompt and add it yourself in Canva or your editor — it'll be sharper and faster.
- **Vague prompts.** "A nice background" gives you something generic. **"Watercolor peonies, pink and gold, birthday mood, square"** gives you something usable.
- **Stopping after the first round.** The first four images are a starting point, not the finish line. If they're close, ask for one specific change. The second round is usually the keeper.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next birthday invite, save-the-date, or holiday card can be made in the time it takes to brew coffee — no software to install, no design skills needed.
- **For your business or work:** social posts, internal event flyers, or vision-board slides for team workshops can be created on the fly. If you batch three or four prompts in one sitting, you have a week's worth of visuals before lunch.
- **If you're just getting started:** open Copilot today and try the birthday invite example from Step 2. Once you've made one, every future prompt is easier.

## Try it now
Open **copilot.microsoft.com**, switch to image mode, and type: *"A dreamy watercolor vision board image with a calm beach at sunrise, a notebook, a cup of coffee, and soft pastel colors, no text."* Save the result you like best. That's your first custom picture — made in under five minutes.
